definitions.explanation: Used when something valuable is wasted or lost, or when a good opportunity is missed.
Used when someone nearly succeeds at something but falls short.

examples.english: Time is precious. / I don't want to waste time.

examples.japanese: あんな{才能|さいのう}を{無駄|むだ}にするのは{惜|お}しい。
examples.english: It's a shame to waste such talent.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}くして{亡|な}くなったのは{惜|お}しい。
examples.english: It's regrettable that they passed away so young.

examples.japanese: {惜|お}しい！もう{少|すこ}しだった。
examples.english: So close! You almost had it.

examples.japanese: {答|こた}えは{惜|お}しかったけど、{間違|まちが}いだ。
examples.english: The answer was close, but wrong.

examples.japanese: あと{一点|いってん}で{優勝|ゆうしょう}だったのに、{惜|お}しかった。
examples.english: We were just one point away from winning - so close.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時間|じかん}が{惜|お}しい: time is precious
- {命|いのち}が{惜|お}しい: one's life is dear
- {金|かね}が{惜|お}しい: reluctant to spend money

USAGE NOTE:
{惜|お}しい！ as an exclamation means "So close!" and is commonly used in sports and games.
